keys.record.qr.disabled.body: It is off for this template or for this organisation, so this document cannot be given a code. The switch is an organisation setting, and a template can opt out of it on its own.
keys.record.qr.disabled.stillHonoured: It has been switched off since this code was issued. The code below is still honoured, and documents issued from now on will not be given one.
keys.record.qr.disabled.title: QR verification is switched off here
keys.record.qr.error.load: Failed to read this document's verification code
keys.record.qr.error.mint: The verification code could not be issued
keys.record.qr.error.switchedOff: QR verification has been switched off for this template or this organisation, so no code can be issued.
keys.record.qr.error.withdraw: The verification code could not be withdrawn
keys.record.qr.mintDialog.printBody: Issuing a code does not re-render this document. The new code appears on versions issued from now on, so nothing in circulation carries it until a corrected version is issued.
keys.record.qr.mintDialog.printTitle: Paper already printed does not change
keys.record.qr.mintDialog.retiresBody: Reference {reference} is retired the moment this succeeds. Every copy already printed carries it, and scanning one will no longer confirm this document.
keys.record.qr.mintDialog.retiresTitle: The current code stops being honoured
keys.record.qr.mintDialog.subtitle: A code identifies this document so anyone can confirm it is genuine. It never grants access to it.
keys.record.qr.mintDialog.titleRotate: Issue a new verification code for “{title}”?
keys.record.qr.noSymbol: The symbol and its address are not shown: this installation has not been told its own public address, so it cannot say what the printed code carries.
keys.record.qr.none: This document does not carry a verification code. Issuing one gives it a symbol anyone can scan to confirm it is genuine — it appears on versions issued from now on, and copies already printed are unchanged.
keys.record.qr.readOnly.permission: You can see this document’s verification code and how often it has been scanned. Issuing a new one, or withdrawing it, needs a capability your account does not have.
keys.record.qr.readOnly.record: No verification code can be issued for this document as things stand. The reason is below.
keys.record.qr.retired.title: Codes this document no longer honours
keys.record.qr.retired.why: Kept so somebody holding an older printing can be told which code it carries, and when it stopped being honoured.
keys.record.qr.scans.none: This document has not been scanned.
keys.record.qr.scans.privacy: A scan records the act, not the visitor. For a public scan nothing about the scanner is stored — no address, no device, no location — because there is no column that could hold it. Repeat scans of the same code within a minute count once, so this is a record of scans rather than of page views.
keys.record.qr.scans.refusedNote: “Not confirmed” means the code had already been withdrawn or replaced when it was scanned, so the public page did not confirm the document.
keys.record.qr.stranded.body: Reference {reference} was retired {when} when a newer code was issued, but this document is not carrying one now.
keys.record.qr.stranded.bodyPlain: Reference {reference} was retired when a newer code was issued, but this document is not carrying one now.
keys.record.qr.stranded.title: No code is in force
keys.record.qr.subtitle: A printed code lets anyone confirm this document is genuine. It identifies the document; it never grants access to it.
keys.record.qr.title: Verification code
keys.record.qr.unconfigured.body: A verification code encodes a web address, and nobody has told this installation its own. Until an operator sets APP_URL, a code issued here would lead nowhere.
keys.record.qr.unconfigured.title: This installation has no public address
keys.record.qr.whatItDoes: Scanning it opens a public page that confirms this document is genuine and names this organisation. The page shows no content, no recipients and nobody’s name — and it grants nothing: somebody who may not read this document is refused exactly as they are today, whether or not they hold the paper.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.finalBody: A code can never be un-withdrawn. Issuing one later creates a different code; it does not bring this one back, and it does not change paper that is already printed.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.paper: All {versions} issued versions of this document carry this code. Every copy already printed keeps the symbol and stops confirming anything.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.paperOne: The one issued version of this document carries this code. Every copy already printed keeps the symbol and stops confirming anything.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.scanner: Anyone who scans it from now on — a courier, a clerk, somebody holding your letter — is refused a confirmation.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.scans: {count} scans of it are already recorded.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.scansNone: No scan of this code has been recorded yet.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.scansOne: One scan of it is already recorded.
keys.record.qr.withdrawDialog.title: Withdraw the verification code from “{title}”?
keys.record.qr.withdrawn.consequence: Every copy already printed still carries that symbol, and scanning one no longer confirms anything. A withdrawal cannot be reversed — issuing a code now creates a different one and does not bring this back.
keys.record.qr.withdrawn.plainBy: Reference {reference} stopped being honoured, withdrawn by {who}.
keys.record.qr.withdrawn.title: This code was withdrawn
keys.record.qr.withdrawn.whenBy: Reference {reference} stopped being honoured {when}, withdrawn by {who}.
keys.record.recipients.closed: {count} already acted on it. What each of them did is in the trail below.
keys.record.recipients.none: This document has not been sent to anyone, so nobody is holding it.
keys.record.recipients.readOnly.record: This document is not awaiting you. You are reading it as a record rather than as something to act on.
keys.record.recipients.settled: Nobody is holding this document. Everyone it reached has acted on it.
keys.record.recipients.subtitle: Everyone a route reached who has not acted yet. A row closes when they do.
keys.record.recipients.title: Where it is now
keys.record.recipients.youBody: It is on your list until you act on it. Forwarding, acknowledging and returning are done from your inbox, which is the one place those actions live.
keys.record.subtitle: Issued from {template}
keys.record.trail.none: Nothing has been recorded against this document. A trail begins when it is sent into a route, and every step it takes is appended here.
keys.record.trail.pastEnd: There are no entries on this page of the trail.
keys.record.trail.readOnly.record: This document has not been put into circulation, so nothing has happened to it yet.
keys.record.trail.subtitle: Append-only. An entry is never edited or removed — a correction is a new entry.
keys.record.trail.title: What has happened to it
keys.routing.act.decision.approved.ends: Approved. This step is approved, and the route names nowhere for it to go next — so the document goes no further along this chain.
keys.routing.act.decision.approved.moved: Approved. This step is approved and the document has moved on: the step it went to resolved to {resolved} people and reached {delivered}.
keys.routing.act.decision.heading: Your decision on this route
keys.routing.act.decision.item: Step {position} is a decision step, and it is asking you to approve or reject. Where the document goes next follows from your verdict rather than from a destination you choose.
keys.routing.act.decision.pending.approved: Your approval is recorded. This step is not approved yet — it is still waiting on the other people it was put to.
keys.routing.act.decision.pending.rejected: Your rejection is recorded. This step is not settled yet — under its approval rule the people who have not answered can still carry it.
keys.routing.act.decision.rejected.ends: Rejected. This step can no longer be approved, and the route draws no path for a rejection — so the document goes no further along this chain. A rejection never falls through to where an approval would have sent it.
keys.routing.act.decision.rejected.moved: Rejected. This step can no longer be approved, and the document has gone where the route sends a rejection: that step resolved to {resolved} people and reached {delivered}.
keys.routing.act.delivered: This route sent you the document. You were not asked to act on it, so it is not waiting on you.
keys.routing.act.delivered.heading: This route sent you the document
keys.routing.act.deliveredAtStep: Step {position} sent you the document. You were not asked to act on it, so it is not waiting on you.
keys.routing.act.denied.decisionStep: Step {position} is a decision step: it is answered with a verdict, and where the document goes next follows from that verdict. Forwarding would let you choose the destination the step exists to decide.
keys.routing.act.denied.delivered: This route sent you the document rather than asking you for anything, so there is nothing here to answer. You can still add a note.
keys.routing.act.denied.firstStep: This item came from the first step of the route, so there is no earlier recipient to return it to. Acknowledge it, or add a note explaining the problem.
keys.routing.act.denied.lastStep: This is the last step of the route, so there is nothing to forward to. Acknowledge it instead.
keys.routing.act.denied.noOpenItem: You have no open item on this route. An item you have already acted on cannot be acted on again — add a note instead, which appends to the trail without changing what happened.
keys.routing.act.error: The action could not be recorded.
keys.routing.act.error.network: The action could not be sent.
keys.routing.act.forwarded.ok: Recorded. The next step resolved to {resolved} people and reached {delivered}.
keys.routing.act.heading: Your action on this route
keys.routing.act.item: You have an open item at step {position}.
keys.routing.act.itemUnknownStep: You have an open item on this route.
keys.routing.act.noItem: Nothing on this route is awaiting you. You can still add a note — the trail has no edit path, so a correction is appended beside what it corrects.
keys.routing.act.note.decisionLabel: Reason (optional, appended to the trail beside your verdict)
keys.routing.act.note.label: Note (optional, appended to the trail)
keys.routing.act.noted.needsText: A note needs some text to append.
keys.routing.act.quorum.all: Every one of them must approve. One rejection settles it, because unanimity is impossible after that.
keys.routing.act.quorum.any: One approval from any of them carries it, so yours may settle it on its own. A rejection decides nothing while anybody is still able to approve.
keys.routing.act.quorum.cohort: This step was put to {count} people at once.
keys.routing.act.quorum.inherited: That is this tenant’s rule for approval steps; this step does not override it.
keys.routing.act.quorum.majority: It is approved when more than half of them approve, and refused as soon as a majority in favour has become impossible.
keys.routing.act.quorum.onStep: This step names that rule itself.
keys.routing.badId.description: The address does not name a document.
keys.routing.badId.title: Not a document
keys.routing.compose.blocked.incomplete: Step {position} still needs a rule and its setting.
keys.routing.compose.blocked.noSteps: A route needs at least one step. A route with none would issue a document to nobody and record it as sent.
keys.routing.compose.error: The route could not be created.
keys.routing.compose.error.network: The route could not be sent.
keys.routing.compose.group.previewError: Who this group reaches could not be worked out.
keys.routing.compose.group.previewNetworkErro: Who this group reaches could not be worked out.
keys.routing.compose.groups.error: User groups could not be loaded.
keys.routing.compose.groups.forbidden: You cannot list user groups here, so a step cannot name one. An administrator would need to grant you permission to read user groups.
keys.routing.compose.groups.forbiddenNamed: You cannot list user groups here, so a step cannot name one. An administrator would need to grant you {slug}.
keys.routing.compose.groups.partial: Only some user groups could be loaded, so this list may be incomplete.
keys.routing.compose.heading: Choose the steps this document follows
keys.routing.compose.issued: Route created. Its first step resolved to {resolved} people and reached {delivered}.
keys.routing.compose.issuedEmpty: Route created, but its first step resolved to nobody — no active member holds that role. Nothing is awaiting anyone.
keys.routing.compose.noRules: This installation has no routing rules registered, so a route cannot name anybody. Core provides two; a plugin can add more.
keys.routing.compose.people.forbidden: You cannot list people here, so a step cannot name one by name. An administrator would need to grant you permission to read people.
keys.routing.compose.people.forbiddenNamed: You cannot list people here, so a step cannot name one by name. An administrator would need to grant you {slug}.
keys.routing.compose.people.partial: Only some people could be loaded, so this list may be incomplete.
keys.routing.compose.preview.contract: Each step names a RULE, not people. Who it reaches is worked out when the document is sent — and for every step after the first, relative to whoever forwards it. You will be told how many people the first step reached as soon as the route is created.
keys.routing.compose.roles.forbidden: You cannot list roles here, so a rule cannot name one. An administrator would need to grant you permission to read roles.
keys.routing.compose.roles.forbiddenNamed: You cannot list roles here, so a rule cannot name one. An administrator would need to grant you {slug}.
keys.routing.compose.roles.partial: Only some roles could be loaded, so this list may be incomplete.
keys.routing.compose.step.delivery: Send without asking — everybody this step reaches is told, their item closes immediately, and the route continues.
keys.routing.compose.step.groupDynamic: A group is a rule, not a saved list of people. Who it reaches is worked out again every time the document moves, so this is what it means right now — not a set that has been fixed in place.
keys.routing.compose.step.groupPreviewEmpty: This group resolves to nobody right now. A step naming it would reach no one.
keys.routing.compose.step.groupPreviewLoading: Working out who this group reaches…
keys.routing.compose.step.groupPreviewSample: Showing {shown} of the {total} — a sample, not the whole set:
keys.routing.compose.step.groupUnknown: This step names user group #{id}, which is not in the list you can see — it may have been deleted, or you may not be able to read it. Choosing another group here would replace it.
keys.routing.compose.step.label: Label shown on the step (optional)
keys.routing.compose.step.noGroups: No user groups have been defined here yet. An administrator can define one under User Groups, and a step can then name it.
keys.routing.compose.step.noPeople: There is nobody here to name.
keys.routing.compose.step.noRoles: No roles are available to name.
keys.routing.compose.step.peopleHelp: This step means exactly these people and nobody else — it will not pick up somebody who joins later. For a set that keeps up with the organisation, name a user group instead.
keys.routing.compose.step.peopleMoreMatches: Showing {shown} of {total} matches — keep typing to narrow it down.
keys.routing.compose.step.pluginConfig: This rule is configured by the plugin that provides it. It will be sent with no settings; if it needs some, the server will say which.
keys.routing.compose.template.blocked.none: Choose a route template to apply.
keys.routing.compose.template.label: Route template
keys.routing.compose.template.loadError: This route template could not be read.
keys.routing.compose.template.none: No route templates have been designed here yet. Somebody who may design flows can draw one under Route Templates, and it can then be applied to any document.
keys.routing.compose.template.snapshot: The design is copied onto the document as it stands right now. Redrawing it afterwards will not move a circulation already under way — but each stage still names a RULE, so who it reaches is worked out when the document gets there.
keys.routing.compose.templates.error: Route templates could not be loaded.
keys.routing.compose.templates.forbidden: You cannot read this tenant’s route templates, so a design cannot be applied here. An administrator would need to grant you permission to read route templates.
keys.routing.compose.templates.forbiddenNamed: You cannot read this tenant’s route templates, so a design cannot be applied here. An administrator would need to grant you {slug}.
keys.routing.compose.templates.partial: Only some route templates could be loaded, so this list may be incomplete.

keys.routing.compose.title.helpTemplate: Left blank, the route is named after the template it follows.
keys.routing.compose.title.label: Route name (optional)
keys.routing.description: Where this document has been sent, and what you can do about it.
keys.routing.empty.description: It has no route, so nobody has been asked to act on it and there is nothing in its trail. Sending it creates a route: an ordered set of steps, each naming a rule rather than a person.
keys.routing.empty.title: This document has not been circulated
keys.routing.error.document: This document could not be loaded.
keys.routing.error.recipients: The recipients of this document could not be loaded.
keys.routing.error.routes: This document’s routes could not be loaded.
keys.routing.error.rules: The routing rules could not be loaded.
keys.routing.fanout.chains.heading: Branches
keys.routing.fanout.chains.none: This route reached nobody. Its first step resolved to an empty set of people — the rule found no one holding that role.
keys.routing.fanout.independent: These branches move independently — each recipient resolves the next step relative to themselves, so one branch can finish while another has not been opened. There is no single step the document as a whole is "on".
keys.routing.fanout.open: {people} awaiting action, across {steps} of this route’s steps.
keys.routing.fanout.settled: Nobody has this open. Every chain of this route has been acted on.
keys.routing.fanout.settledDelivered: Nobody has this open. Every chain of this route has been delivered.
keys.routing.fanout.settledMixed: Nobody has this open. Every chain of this route is closed.
keys.routing.fanout.steps.heading: Steps, and who each one reached
keys.routing.names.partial: People’s names could not all be loaded, so some recipients are shown by id.

keys.verify.genuineBody: It was issued by the organisation named below, on the date shown.
